CHARLES M. HALL, Nu Alpha '71

A New President at the Helm
Charles
My chief aim as President will be to
build on 157 years of growth and tradition
so that Psi Upsilon will be ready for the
21st Century." With these words, Chailes
M, Hall, Nu Alpha '71, took office in De
cember 1990, as President of the Exec
utive Council of Psi Upsilon Fraternity,
Brother Hall becomes the Fraternity's
18th president, succeeding William R,
Robie, Epsilon Omega '66, who served
from 1984 until 1990,
Brother Hall has been active in Psi Up
silon since his undergraduate days at
Washington and Lee University where
he was president of the Nu Alpha ChapM. Hall, Nu Alpha 71, Gamma
ter. After earning a Reserve Commission
in the U,S. Army as an Air Defense Ar
tillery Officer and completing his active
duty service, Brother Hall continued his
education and his activity in Psi Upsilon,
In 1974, while attending the Emory Uni
versity Lamar School of Law, he was
elected to the Executive Council, In 1982
he became Finance Chairman and he
served as Treasurer of the Council from
1984 until 1990,
Brother Hall has also been very active
in the Psi Upsilon Society of Georgia,
Inc, (PUSOG), the alumni corporation of
the Gamma Tau Chapter at Georgia Tech.
He presently serves as Treasurer of
PUSOG and was its President from 1978
to 1982, In 1990 he was elected as Hon
orary Gamma Tau in recognition of his
nearly 20 years as an unofficial Chapter
Advisor.
Born in South Charleston, West Vir
ginia, he grew up in Williamstown in that
state, where his parents still live. Chuck,
as he is known to his friends, now lives
in Atlanta where he is very involved in
his community.
Brother Hall is an attorney in private
practice and is affiliated with a small firm.
When he is not working for Psi U, Chuck
concentrates on corporate and contract
law and contract litigation. For recrea
tion he enjoys skiing, weight-lifting, run
ning and reading.
Brother Hall also finds time to be ac
tive in the Atlanta community. He was a
member of the Atlanta Junior Chamber
of Commerce, which was one ofthe larg-
'90H
est Jaycee Chapters in the U.S,, and was
twice named Committee Chairman ofthe
Year, He also served terms as Director
and General Counsel.
He was twice elected President ofthe
Buckhead Northside Civitan Club, and
next year will serve for a second time as
Civitan District Judge Advocate for
Northern Georgia.
Brother Hall serves as a volunteer
Trustee and Treasurer of the Georgia
Dental Education Foundation, and as
Trustee and Vice-President of Manage
ment and Operations of Annandale Vil
lage, a residential care facility for the
mentally handicapped in Suwanee,
Georgia.
Brother Hall has traveled extensively
in North America for Psi Upsilon and has
visited almost all Chapters of the Fra
ternity. He expects to complete his tour
of Psi Upsilon before he retires as Pres
ident. His most memorable travel ex
perience though was seven days in a tent
at several primitive camp sites in East
Africa in 1988, Brother Hall, who has
visited the Third World before, and who
has a younger brother who lives in Africa,
says that his opportunity to spend time
hving under difficult conditions helped
him understand the wonderful advan
tages that life in North America affords.
Chuck's first commitment is to his Fra
ternity and he is eager to see Psi U grow
and prosper, as it continues to foster the
spirit of brotherhood and the high degree
of moral, social and academic excellence
for which it is known.

SIGMA (1840)
Brown University
These past two semesters have been a
time of growth and building for the Sigma,
Last year saw a
complete upheaval of our ed
ucation process, during which we officially
abohshed pledging. Come September we had
to feel our way through the new education
program, since we were essentially starting
from scratch. While there were certainly flaws
in our design and difficulties in its execution,
the new
program went very well on the whole.
One of the Sigma's primary commit
ments has always been to community service,
both inside and outside the Brown commu
nity. This year, thanks to a newly-instituted
service program, we have been particularly
successful: our house of less than fifty mem
bers has logged over 900 hours of service since
September, Because of this, we have high
hopes of receiving the Greek Council Award
for Community Service for the 1990-1991 ac
ademic year.
One area which has not been strong is
alumni relations. We are now attempting to
reaffirm old ties and forge new ones, both with
the brothers ofthe Sigma ofthe past, and with
the brothers of the Sigma of the present. We
encourage all Sigma and Psi Upsilon alumni
to stop in at the house whenever in the Prov
idence area,
Eric Masters '92
President
GAMMA (1841)
Amherst College
The year began rather smoothly with
renovations performed on our small house.
Originally, we wanted to extend our chapter
room due to the ever
increasing number of
Gamma brothers. However, due to town reg
ulations, we could only enlarge the living room.
Brother Brian Beebe '93 also helped to max
imize the space of the house by cleaning out
the basement of 30 Railroad Street, or the
Lodge as we affectionately call it. The in
creased area provides for more comfortable
meetings.
During the spring, we had two major
events, the Psi U Gamma semi-formal, Gammv
Prom, and our spring rush. Both events went
extremely well. The Gammy Prom was held
at the Hotel .Northhampton. We all piled into
a school bus on
Saturday evening and pro
ceeded to sing for the entire bus ride over.
Dinner and dancing lasted until 11:30,
We expect that the strength of the
Gamma chapter will continue to grow, as the
underclassmen possess an enthusiasm which
can only help the Chapter flourish. The vi
tality of the undergraduates combined with
the great support offered by the alumni makes
the continued success of the Gamma inevi
table,
Steven M, Vitale '91
Past President
ZETA (1842)
Dartmouth College
The Zeta Chapter has continued to
strive for excellence at Dartmouth College,
We successfully endured the rigors of the
Minimum Standards Review by the College
in the Fall and the financial strains of the de
layed rush policy imposed by the administra
tion. The Winter term offered a more
prom
ising oudook for our Chapter, We gained an
additional 24 new members and remain one
ofthe strongest houses on campus. These new
members promise to uphold the spirit of Psi
Upsilon that has allowed us to maintain our
strong position on campus for the past century
and a half
The entire Greek system at Dartmouth
is currently under fire as the delayed rush
process takes its toll on a number of weaker
houses on campus. Additionally, new univer
sity policies are being drafted to assure that
all Greek organizations comply with new Fed
eral legislation regarding underage alcohol
consumption.
With Seniors anxiously awaiting grad
uation, they reflect on the importance that Psi
Upsilon has had as an integral part of their
Dartmouth experience. During this difficult
period of transition we are now
experiencing,
we
hope to maintain these values that we have
felt so sacred to the Zeta Chapter, We con
tinue to be a
strong leader on
campus, as well
as in the entire Dartmouth community, and
are confident that our
strength will prevail
through the years,
Jeff Guylay '92
President

No report received,
KAPPA (1843)
Bowdoin College
This has been a
year of growth and
change for the Kappa Chapter, We returned
last fall to a renovated kitchen. Thanks to Les
ter Prue, and several Kappas who spent the
summer working, not only was the kitchen
renovated, but we managed to finish up the
last renovations specified by physical plant and
fire code. New windows were installed in the
kitchen, two new counter tops were built, and
a number of cabinets were added. The largest
change in the kitchen was the creation of a
new entry way from the dining room.
Rush went extremely well and the
Kappa now has twenty-eight new members.
The new members have already shown their
enthusiasm, several being elected to executive
positions.
This spring the Kappa held its annual
Bear Aid concert on the Bowdoin Quad, We
redirected the aim of the charity event and
this year raised money or the Merrymeeting
AIDS Support Services, All in all, it has been
a good year and the Kappa continues to grow
in many positive ways.
Josh Lawler '93
President

XI (1843)
Wesleyan University
Adjustment to a new relationship be
tween the fraternities and Wesleyan Univer
sity has characterized the year for the Xi Chap
ter, The University, after continued efforts to
force the all-male houses to coeducate, has
adopted a more moderate plan. As of tiie be
ginning of Spring Semester 1991 University
support for single sex fraternities has been
withdrawn. The Xi Chapter has committed to
remaining single-sex.
The membership of the Xi is truly
flourishing this year. With the addition of 18
new members in the fall, our size has in
creased to 65 undergraduates. The Xi Brothers
occupy important positions in many aspects of
the University, We have a resident advisor,
tour guides, senior interviewers, and the sen
ior class president as Xi Brothers, In addition,
with members of the varsity soccer, cross
country, squash, swimming, basketball, ten
nis, volleyball, baseball, and lacrosse teams as
well as a few varsity captains and All-American
athletes, the Xi continues to exhibit its high
level of athletic excellence. Clearly Xi mem
bers are
playing important roles in the Wes
leyan community, as well as within the house.

IOTA (1860)
Kenyon College
With the College's recent decision to
decrease our housing space, the Lodge will
assume an increasingly important role for the
Iota, as it will provide a
place for the Brothers
to maintain their unity. The Brothers have
realized this and are
making a concerted effort
to bring the Lodge back from the brink of
dilapidation and restore its rustic splendor.
Largely through the efforts of Brother
Dick Penn '49, the Lodge will soon have a
refmished floor, revamped plumbing, and a
new furnace. Brother Penn's work has lead to
a dramatic increase in the Chapter's alumni
support. The undergraduates are extremely
grateful for the help we have received in se
curing the future of the Lodge.
With a
twenty member pledge class,
the Iota will double its size for the coming
year. An enthusiastic and diverse group, the
pledges represent a bright future for the Iota,
Our Community service program has
been greatly expanded. The Brothers are cur
rently involved with the rehabilitation of ju
venile offenders in the Mohican Youth Center,
Also, the Chapter has recently undertaken the
support of an
underprivileged child in the West
Bank, This spring, the Ohio Department of
Highways has officially recognized the Iota as
a
part of its "Adopt a
Highway" program, en
trusting the maintenance of a two mile stretch
of Route 229 to the Chapter,
In the classroom, the Iota finished the
first semester third among fraternities. The
creation ofthe position of Academic Chair for
the Chapter has formalized our dedication to
the intellectual side of the Kenyon Experi
ence,
The coming years should prove suc
cessful for the Iota, Continued alumni sup
port, coupled with an enthusiastic undergrad
uate body, will insure that Psi Upsilon
continues to maintain a strong presence at
Kenyon,
Philip E, Wilson Jr, '91
Past President

OMEGA (1869)
University of Chicago
Greetings from the Omega! The Chap
ter IS
currently on a
long awaited upswing and
moving toward a
brighter future. We have just
uutmted 9 new brothers after an accelerated
pledge education period. The Chapter is also
anticipating a
spring pledge class of compa
rable size.
Moreover, the Omega was able to
recruit the most new members of any frater
nity at the
University of Chicago!
The Chapter held its annual Valentine
Formal with numerous area alumni in attend
ance. The house was
magnificently decorated
and the big-band music was a welcome change
to the customary dance music. Under the di
rection of our Board of Trustees, the chapter
has also adopted a more responsible social pol
icy.
The condition of the house is slowly
improving, with the completion of the new
bathrooms and the replacement of the aged
back stairs, A new
project for the improve
ment ofthe physical shape ofthe house is the
Trustee/Active workday where we have worked
on numerous projects such as
retiling the floor,
repairing light fixtures, and painting. The
chapter is also pleased to announce that we
now have a common lounge area where the
brothers can watch cable television, play mu
sic, relax on new sofas and chairs, or take ad
vantage ofthe pool table.
On a sad note, I must report that our
housemother for 15 years, Mrs, Marjorie Law
rence, could not finish the quarter due to ill
ness and is resting with her sister. The un
dergraduates and numerous alumni feel a bitter
sadness. Our thoughts and prayers are with
Mrs, Lawrence,
Overall, this was a
very trying, never
theless, productive year for the Omega that
made all Brothers realize the importance of
being a
responsible Psi U,
Edgar E, Bueno '91
President

No report received,
CHI (1876)
Cornell University
This Spring at the Chi has been ex
traordinarily eventful, as
always, due to fra
temity education. Thirteen new members were
initiated into the Brotherhood on April 7th,
They will replace 16 graduating Brothers as
the new members join the active Brotherhood
of 46,
Cornell's intramural program contin
ues to provide an outlet for teamwork and
comraderie, highlighted by Psi U victories in
swimming, second place in water polo, and an
impressive showing in the soccer playoffs.
The active brotherhood boasts a tre
mendous amount of Cornefl involvement in
cluding the Chairman of the prestigious Quill
and Dagger Club and Co-Chairman of the
Senior Class Tower Club, In addition, the Chi
offers leadership to numerous varsity sports.
As the Inter-fraternity Council gains
greater importance within Cornell's Greek
System, the Chi is increasing its involvement.
Our involvement includes Director of Mem
bership Enrollment, Chief Justice of the Ju
dicial Board, and an IFC representative. In
an effort to improve inter-fraternity commu
nications, the Chi wifl host a president's re
ception for all undergraduate Greek leaders.
As we
wrap up another year, it is dif
ficult to part with the old, yet this year's suc
cess only foreshadows the strong potential of
the Chi's future,
Harry Pflueger '92
President
BETA BETA (1880)
Trinity College
The Beta Beta Chapter of Psi Upsilon
is having a
prosperous year. Our Brotherhood
has been strengthened with the addition of 14
new members and 7 pledges to the ranks of
Psi Upsilon, The new members are quite ac
tive on
campus, as the group is represented
in six varsity sports.
House improvements are always un
derway because of the age of the Beta Beta
house. Brothers have painted the interior, retiled the basement, and installed a new back
door, A brand new electrical system was in
stalled in the fall, resulting in a safer house.
The Brothers are currently planning to replace
old windows and install new insulation.
Alumni relations are on the upswing at
the Beta Beta, Our newsletter circulation has
increased, as well as alumni response. We are
stressing more mutual alumni involvement in
the near future.
Recently, eight Beta Beta's contrib
uted to an E,C,A,C, North/South hockey
championship. Trinity edged Fitchburg State
4-3 in overtime to end their 35 game North/
South winning streak,
Richard Jay Getzoff '92
President
ETA (1884)
Lehigh University
Greetings from the Eta, This past year
can best be described as a year of change. In
an effort to reduce their risk exposure, the
thirty fraternities at Lehigh adopted a closed
party policy. This policy limits party size and
prevents uninvited party crashers from dam
aging the houses and endangering guests. In
summation, this policy gives fraternities more
control over their parties.
There has also been a policy of Greek
Life Standards adopted for the Lehigh Cam
pus, These standards cover academics, social
development, community relations, pledging,
finances, rush, and leadership development.
Some of the changes include a school wide
minimum GPA in order to affiliate with a fra
ternity, two community service projects per
year, and hosting of a social development pro
gram each semester.
Through the high ideals of Psi Upsilon
and adherence to these new policies, we will

be able to demonstrate the excellence which
the Fraternity system brings out in its mem
bers. The good news must be spread, I look
forward to another 157 -I- years of Psi Upsilon,
so let's keep our eyes open for opportunities.
Kevin P, Mostek '92
Past President

OMICRON (1910)
University of Illinois
The Brothers of the Omicron are
cap
ping off a fine school year marked by an ex
cellent rush effort, vast improvement to the
chapter house, and outstanding community
involvement.
First and foremost, we would like to
welcome back Dan Peterson '94 from his serv
ice in the Army, Dan, who is 21, had served
in Panama prior to college. He was suddenly
recalled for active duty in January, With the
end of the war, Dan is being sent back to iis
after fulfilling his duty to our country. The
Omicron is proud and fortunate to have a man
like Dan in its ranks.
Our Fall Rush Chairmen, David Ko
'92,5 and Bill Cornfield '93, organized a sched
ule of open houses which demonstrated their
creativity under the liberalized Rush format.
We hosted a group of comedians, had a
pig
roast on the front lawn, and treated the rushees to a fine banquet with Brother Carl Beck,
Delta '41, as the guest of honor. All of our
hard work paid off as we initiated 15 fine men
in January,
Our chapter house is occupied to ca
pacity, and the Brothers are enjoying a revi
talized Beta Chi and a beautiful '28 Room, The
Beta Chi received a new ceramic floor and a
fresh coat of paint, while the Red Room got
the rich garnet carpeting it had deserved for
years. The '28 Room benefitted from an out
standing alumni fundraiser and had a locking
glass display case installed. The undergradu
ates heartily thank all of our alumni for their
generous support, with special recognition to
Charles Fish '28 on his induction into the
"Founder's Society,"
313 E, Armory has also been the dinner
host to many distinguished professors, includ
ing history professor Robert W,Johannsen, a
contributor to the recent PBS series on the
Civil War, Our most impressive guest to date
was Champaign Mayor Daniel McCoflum,
David Komie '92
Past President
THETA THETA (1916)
University of Washington
Only good news comes from the Theta
Theta, here at the University of Washington,
Topping our list is the commencement of a
$300,000 renovation project. Beginning in
June, the remodeling viill bring a much needed
face lift to the existing structure. The following
summer will bring phase II of the project,
which will add another $400,000 to the house.
Among campus activities, the Theta
Theta pulled off an unprecedented triple
crown. Victories in Greek Week, Anchor
Splash and the Intramural Sports Champi
onship displayed Psi U's athletic dominance,
as well as the strength ofthe Brotherhood,
1991 is a special year for the Theta
Theta, since it is the 75th, or "Diamond" an
niversary, A special Founders Night party and
dinner banquet is planned to take place in the
Chapter House in the Fall, This would be an
excellent opportunity to view the new reno
vation, as well as share in the Brotherhood of
the Theta Theta of Psi Upsilon,
John Tribble '92
President
NU (1920)
University of Toronto
In the 11th year since its reactivation,
the Nu Chapter maintains a stable presence
on campus. The feeling of being close friends
in conjunction with brotherhood is the main
stay of the chapter's longevity.
Despite the concern over a poor fall
rush, the Nu more than compensated for this
problem with an enormously successfi.il spring
rush.
The relationship with the alumni as
sociation continues to grow stronger through
its advice and support. Having been a member
of the chapter since 1986, 1 have seen the
improvements to the chapter house and the
intellectual grovrth of the chapter. Although
unable to occupy the same house as the former
chapter members, I would like to extend an
invitation to the alumni to visit the current
chapter house,
Cameron G. Scott '91
Past President
EPSILON PHI (1928)
McGiU University
No report received.
ZETA ZETA (1935)
University of British Columbia
The Zeta Zeta Chapter had another ex
citing and growing year at the University of
British Columbia, The year began with a re
treat where the returning brothers were able
to set the short and long term goals for the
chapter. The retreat established a high level
of enthusiasm which was carried throughout
the year to establish Psi Upsilon as one of the
most respected fraternities on campus
�
so
cially, academically and athletically.
The highlight of our year came in
March, at Songfest '91, During this event, fra
ternities and sororities compete in song and
dance and are recognized for their year long
achievements, Psi Upsilon donated the orig
inal trophy but had not participated in the past
11 years. On our return to Songfest compe
tition, the Zeta Zeta was able to capture sec
ond place, with the outstanding musical con
tribution from Brother Richard Jhin '94, This
night was not over yet! Psi Upsilon was also
awarded the Most Improved Fraternity on
campus, and the Most Spirited, Songfest '91
was an
exciting ending to an unforgettable year.
To wrap up the year we held our annual
Hot Tub party where our new friends from
the Beta Kappa Provisional Chapter came up
to visit and experience some Canadian social
life. Our doors are always open and an invi
tation put forth to all our brothers across the
continent to come and experience the Zeta
Zeta hospitality.
D. Wayne Best '92
President
EPSILON NU (1943)
Michigan State University
The Epsflon Nu Chapter of Psi Upsilon
Fraternity continues to forge a lasting impres
sion on campus and community life in East
Lansing. Two successful recruitment efforts in
the Fall and Winter Terms have led to the
induction of fourteen worthy gentlemen into
our ranks. The Spring term brought 3 more
new members.
Later this Spring, Michigan State Uni
versity, along vrith the Greek system, vrill once
again welcome the Special Olympics to our
campus for their annual meet. The Epsilon
Nu Chapter promises to have an active par
ticipatory hand in this year's meet in light of
our unmatched fundraising efforts for Special
Olympics this winter. Campus wide recogni
tion of the Chapter's philanthropic efforts has
been a source of great pride for the active
members, and has subsequently furthered
community interests. The Alumni Board has
initiated fundraising efforts of its own to fi
nance the necessary improvements on the
Chapter House, The success of these efforts
hinges on the complete and generous support
of all active and alumni Brothers,
Tradition, leadership, extracurricular
activities, academics, and brotherhood con
tinue to be the foundations ofthe Epsilon Nu,

of PSI UPSILON 5
and the outlook for the Chapter is unques
tionably bright,
Christopher J, Nelson '92
President

ZETA TAU (1981)
Tufts University
This semester at the Zeta Tau has been
a rebuilding process, which was inevitable.
With our membership down to seventeen
brothers, we initiated one of our laigest groups
yet, eleven. The Zeta Tau is gaining accept
ance by the Inter-Greek System Government
through the chapter's participation in its ac
tivities and willingness to work with it for cer
tain charities. Overall, things are starting to
look up for us here at the Zeta Tau,
John Erickson '92
President
EPSILON IOTA (1982)
Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute
This has been an exciting year for the
Epsilon Iota Chapter, The chapter will be ex
ercising its option to purchase the chapter
house from Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute
in June,
Since we will be purchasing the prop
erty, a tremendous amount of maintenance
has been performed. The garage, which was
formerly inundated with debris, has been
cleaned and emptied. As a community service
project, the chapter spent a day last faO paint
ing the rooms and hallway in a convent in
Menands, New York,
The Epsilon lota's Fall and Spring rush
went
exceptionally well, obtaining 6 and 4 new
members respectively, nearly doubling the
chapter size. With only three brothers grad
uating this Spring, the chapter experienced a
net gain of seven. With seven members grad
uating next spring, the Epsilon Iota looks for
ward to another successful year of member
ship recruitment,
Michael Lobo '92
President
PHI BETA (1984)
College of William and Mary
The 1990-1991 school year has proven
to be one ofthe strongest and most productive
in the seven year history ofthe Phi Beta Chap
ter ofPsi Upsilon, With an active brotherhood
of 53, the Phi Beta continues to grow and
maintain a
hardy presence on
campus, while
at the same time maintaining its reputation for
diversity and excellence.
The Brothers of the Phi Beta helped
the Williamsburg community by once again
volunteering for the Williamsburg Housing
Partnership program. We have also instituted
our own
recycling program. In February, Psi
U took first place in the annual Tri Delta Greek
Decathlon, securing $300 for philanthropic
projects, Psi U also took fourth place in the
Delta Gamma Anchor Splash Competition,
Psi Upsilon has become a haven for
those seeking to dance and socialize, rather
than to just drink, A few of the theme parties
the Phi Beta hosted this year include the first
of what promises to be an annual square dance
party, our second annual Beriin Wall party, a
twister party, and an early eighties revival
party, Psi U (with the help of Phi Mu Sorority)
also placed second in the William and Mary
Homecoming Float Competition,
The Phi Beta welcomes any and all vis
itors to experience Williamsburg,
David L, Bulova '91
Past President
KAPPA PHI (1989)
Pennsylvania State University
No report received,
UPSILON TAU PROVISIONAL
University of Texas at Austin
Greetings from the Upsilon Tau Pro
visional Chapter! We at the Upsilon Tau have
been working hard throughout the year to ful
fill the Psi Upsilon chapter acceptance stand
ards. We have held strong at the University
of Texas at Austin while racial and hazing in
cidents have plagued others in the fraternity
system.
Rush went well this year with the ad
dition of five new members. We are eagerly
awaiting Fall rush and are working towards
recruiting a strong fall class.
The social scene at the Upsilon Tau has
been going strong aO year long. Some of the
outstanding events included parties with Sigma
Phi Omega sorority and Phi Kappa Theta and
Zeta Psi fraternities. At Greek Week this year,
the Upsilon Tau, the newest fraternity at Texas,
surprised everyone by taking first place in the
volleyball tournament.
During the next year we hope to ac
complish two major goals: to fulfifl the chapter
acceptance procedures and to set up a sports
league at the University ofTexas for the smaller
fraternities. With a great deal of work, we
think we can accomplish both,
William Kaigler '92
President
BETA ALPHA PROVISIONAL
Miami University of Ohio
The academic year 1990-1991 has been
highlighted by success in many areas at the
Beta Alpha Provisional, Our year began when
we took possession of our new chapter house
in August of 1990, The brothers began work
immediately to restore what had become in
recent years a very dilapidated structure.
This year has seen the Brothers of the
Beta Alpha participating in a number of phil
anthropic events, among them Phi Kappa Psi's
Downhill Derby (which we won) and the Delta
Gamma Anchor Splash, We are beginning to
lay the foundation for a
philanthropy of our
own next year.
The year has also been marked by var
ious social events, among them parties with a
number of campus sororities, and our recent
"Just for Laughs!" date party. We enjoyed a
visit from the Brothers of the Iota Chapter in
January and look forward to returning the
compliment soon.
Certainly the highlight of our year has
been winter rush, in which both quantity and
quality of rushees were high. We accepted 9
fine men, placing our
membership after a year
and a half at 38,
We look forward to pursuing our
quest
for a Charter and are always happy to welcome
visiting Brothers of Psi Upsilon to Oxford,
John E, Riemenschneider '91
Corresponding Secretary
BETA KAPPA PROVISIONAL
Washington State University
This has been an excellent year for the
Beta Kappa at Washington State University,
The school year began on the right foot as we
accepted thirteen new men into the fraternity
during our informal rush. Shortly thereafter,
on September 29th, 1990, twenty-nine of us
went through an especially meaningful pledg
ing ceremony. This March we brought in four
more members, bringing our current total
membership to thirty-three.
Socially, the Beta Kappa continues to
be active, participating in a Fall Cruise on lake
Couer D'Alene with Sigma Kappa Sorority, a
Pajama Party with the women of Gamma Phi
Beta, a Valentine Dance with Phi Kappa Tau,
and the Dating Game with Alpha Delta Pi
sorority.
Academically, the Beta Kappa placed
fourth among fraternities on campus for its
first semester at Washington State University,
Chris McDougall had the best grades in the
group with a 3,93 G,P,A,
The Beta Kappa held two Alumni Din
ners �
one in Pullman and one in Spokane,
We had an excellent time and special thanks
are in order for Brother Norman Schoonover,
Theta Theta '46, for his invaluable assistance.
The Beta Kappa welcomes all Psi Upsilon
alumni to stop in at Washington State Uni
versity,
Matthew C, Kelley '93
Secretary

The Providence Chamber of Commerce is fond of saying "Providence harbors the best." Psi Upsilon will
harbor the best ofthe interfraternal world at its 1991 Leadership Institute this summer. A number of distin
guished members of the NIC Commission on Values and Ethics will serve as Leadership Institute faculty.
This year we will examine the meaning of fraternity and the role of confrontation in our program entitled
"Brother or brOther?"
Charles M. Hall, Nu Alpha '71, the 18th President of the Psi Upsilon Executive Council will preside over
the 148th Convention ofthe Fraternity which opens Saturday morning, August 24, 1991. The Convention is
the legislative body of the Fraternity which will set the course for the coming year. Every active chapter of
the Fraternity will be represented by undergraduates and alumni alike. In addition to the working, legislative
sessions, the Convention grants several fraternity awards and provides an opportunity to make or renew
lifelong acquaintances.
